question: When performing a dermographism test, which combination of site, instrument, and observation interval is MOST appropriate?

answers.text: Volar forearm or upper back, using the blunt wooden end of a cotton swab, with the result read at 3–5 minutes

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The volar forearm or upper back are ideal test sites — accessible, relatively hairless, and easy to observe. A blunt object like the wooden end of a cotton swab provides standardised, moderate pressure without abrading the skin. The diagnostic wheal takes 3–5 minutes to develop fully, so this is the correct observation interval.

answers.text: Dorsum of the hand, using a fingernail, with the result read immediately

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A fingernail produces inconsistent pressure and risks abrading the skin, which can create a non-specific mark mistaken for a positive result. The dorsum of the hand is hairier and harder to observe. The wheal develops over 3–5 minutes — reading immediately would miss it entirely.

answers.text: Anterior chest, using repeated light strokes with a pen cap, with the result read after 24 hours

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Repeated light strokes do not provide the single, firm, standardised pressure needed to elicit the response reliably. The dermographic wheal is transient — it develops within minutes and fades within the hour, so a 24-hour reading would find nothing.

answers.text: Lateral thigh, using a cold metal object pressed firmly for 10 seconds, with the result read at 10 minutes

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A cold metal object tests for cold urticaria, not dermographism. Dermographism is elicited specifically by a firm linear stroke — 'writing on the skin' — not by temperature or sustained pressure stimuli.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key elements are: test on the volar forearm or upper back; use a blunt object (not a fingernail) for a single firm linear stroke of moderate, even pressure; and observe the result at 3–5 minutes — the diagnostic wheal takes time to develop.

Good. The three essentials of the dermographism test are: a proper site (volar forearm or upper back), a blunt instrument applied as a single firm linear stroke, and reading the result at 3–5 minutes when the wheal has had time to develop.
